uncited: They set themselves apart from sibling methods by treating grid deformations and topological weights as learnable parameters, enabling the resolution of topological ambiguities and the production of high-fidelity surfaces directly from neural network outputs [S1, S2].
Early work focused on static extraction from NeRF density fields [S1].
The introduction of differentiable extraction, such as MISE [S1], allowed for adaptive sampling.

Subsequent developments like FlexiCubes [S2] and Differentiable Marching Cubes [S2] enabled end-to-end training of geometry by making the extraction process differentiable with respect to grid parameters.
Ground truth generation methods [S1] were developed to train CNNs for fast inference, replacing the differentiable optimization step with a learned approximation.
